problem_statement.title: [BUG] SolverVBD over-allocates body-particle contact buffers in multi-world models
problem_statement.body:
### Bug Description

Constructing `SolverVBD` on a replicated multi-world model allocates body-particle contact buffers sized by the *cross-world* product of the global shape and particle counts. The allocation grows quadratically with world count while the contacts that can actually occur grow linearly, so the over-allocation factor grows linearly. Once the product reaches `2**31` the solver cannot be constructed at all. Single-world models are unaffected (factor is exactly 1).

Expected: the buffers are sized from the capacity the collision pipeline can actually produce, as they already are for rigid contacts.

`_init_rigid_system` ([solver_vbd.py#L826-L827](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L826-L827)):

```python
if model.particle_count > 0 and model.shape_count > 0:
    self._init_body_particle_contact_state(model.shape_count * model.particle_count)
```

`_init_body_particle_contact_state` ([L1167-L1172](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L1167-L1172)) allocates four `wp.zeros(n, dtype=float)` arrays, so 16 bytes per slot.

**This is a stale invariant, not an arbitrary constant.** When it was written it exactly matched the pipeline default. #3118 changed that default and did not update `solver_vbd.py` — CHANGELOG.md:185:

> Change `CollisionPipeline.soft_contact_max` to default to the precomputed `soft_rigid_contact_pair_count` instead of `shape_count * particle_count`; pass `soft_contact_max=model.shape_count * model.particle_count` to preserve the previous capacity. (#3118)

The pipeline now sizes from world-compatible pairs only ([collide.py#L1131-L1136](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/sim/collide.py#L1131-L1136); `_world_compatible_pairs` at [L480-L546](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/sim/collide.py#L480-L546), added later by #3262 — which did edit `solver_vbd.py`, still leaving L826-827 stale).

For `W` worlds each holding `S` world-local shapes and an equal share of particles, plus `G` global (`world == -1`) shapes and no global particles, the over-allocation factor is `(W*S + G) / (S + G)`: linear in `W`, and exactly `W` when `G = 0`, as in the repro below.

**The class docstring already describes the intended behaviour** ([L135-L138](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L135-L138)): *"SolverVBD pre-allocates contact state from capacities populated by `CollisionPipeline` when available; otherwise, the first `step` lazily sizes buffers from `Contacts`."* The rigid path has such a capacity, and `collide.py:908-910` writes it back specifically to keep the two in sync:

```python
# Keep model-level default in sync with the resolved pipeline capacity.
# This avoids divergence between model- and contacts-based users (e.g. VBD init).
model.rigid_contact_max = rigid_contact_max
```

There is no `model.soft_contact_max` anywhere, so the soft path always takes the worst-case branch. For the same reason, constructing the `CollisionPipeline` before the solver does not help the soft path (it does help the rigid one, via the write-back above) — L827 is computed from `model` alone.

**There is no supported way to cap it.** `SolverVBD.__init__` ([L222-L269](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L222-L269)) exposes no soft-contact capacity parameter; `rigid_body_particle_contact_buffer_size` is a per-body list stride, not this global capacity.

**Failure modes.** Below `2**31` slots the allocation succeeds and silently wastes VRAM. For 64 worlds each holding 64 shapes and a 10x10x10-particle soft grid — 4,096 shapes x 64,000 particles = 262,144,000 slots — `SolverVBD` reserves 4.19 GB on an RTX 5090 (measured free-memory delta 4.23 GB) where the pipeline's capacity is 4,096,000 slots = 65.5 MB. At or above `2**31` slots, construction fails outright in Warp's per-dimension int32 shape check (`check_array_shape`, `warp/_src/types.py:2976` in warp 1.17.0.dev20260725, called from `array._init_new` before any device allocation, so it reproduces on CPU):

```
ValueError: Array shapes must not exceed the maximum representable value of a signed 32-bit
integer, got 2166784000 in dimension 0.
```

Output of the reproduction script below (a few seconds on CPU, no GPU required; Warp's init banner and `Module ... load` lines elided):

```
newton 1.5.0.dev0, warp 1.17.0.dev20260725

 worlds  shapes  particles   VBD allocates  pipeline needs  ratio    VBD bytes
      1       8         27             216             216    1.0        3,456
      2      16         54             864             432    2.0       13,824
      4      32        108           3,456             864    4.0       55,296
      8      64        216          13,824           1,728    8.0      221,184
     16     128        432          55,296           3,456   16.0      884,736
     32     256        864         221,184           6,912   32.0    3,538,944
     64     512       1728         884,736          13,824   64.0   14,155,776

worlds=184  shapes=11,776  particles=184,000
SolverVBD wants 2,166,784,000 slots = 34.67 GB; pipeline capacity is 11,776,000 = 188.4 MB
ValueError: Array shapes must not exceed the maximum representable value of a signed 32-bit integer, got 2166784000 in dimension 0.
```

That model has no global shapes, so the `ratio` column equals `world_count` exactly at every row.

**Suggested fix.** Size the preallocation from the pipeline's capacity rather than the dense product. Shrinking looks safe: every index into the four buffers is a flat contact id produced under a launch dimensioned by `contacts.soft_contact_max`. The producer `build_body_particle_contact_lists` ([rigid_vbd_kernels.py:2842](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/rigid_vbd_kernels.py#L2842)) stores `tid` from a launch of that dim ([solver_vbd.py#L2490](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L2490)), and every consumer reads either `wp.tid()` under the same dim (`rigid_vbd_kernels.py:3340`/`:4948`, `particle_vbd_kernels.py:1820`/`:2324`, `vbd_coupling_kernels.py:154`/`:300`) or one of those stored ids (`rigid_vbd_kernels.py:3972`, reached from the per-body launch at `solver_vbd.py:2796-2798`). Nothing indexes them in the `shape_count * particle_count` space. `_initialize_rigid_bodies` also already grows them on demand ([L2473-L2481](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L2473-L2481), [L2512-L2520](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L2512-L2520)).

Two things to watch if the eager path is removed entirely rather than resized: the proxy-coupling harvest hooks at [L1016](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L1016) and [L1077](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L1077) gate, among other conditions, on `shape[0] >= contacts.soft_contact_max` and silently skip the launch when short; and `_raise_if_capturing_resize` ([L1186-L1194](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/solver_vbd.py#L1186-L1194)) turns a needed regrow during graph capture into a `RuntimeError`. Sizing from a real capacity avoids both.

One caveat on direction: with the default `enable_rigid_soft_full_surface_contact=False` the dense product is always an over-estimate, but `collide.py:1134` adds edge/face pair headroom on top, so with that flag enabled at low world counts the pipeline capacity can exceed `shape_count * particle_count` and L827 becomes an *under*-estimate. Measured on the repro model with the flag on, the crossover is between 4 and 8 worlds (1 world: 1,176 vs 216; 8 worlds: 9,408 vs 13,824). Sizing from the pipeline fixes both directions.

**Possibly related.** `newton/_src/solvers/style3d/collision/collision.py:42` has the identical expression, but feeds a `wp.launch` dim ([L203](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/402d8eac02c42243a5c9ae7e4b8f223ca8bf0394/newton/_src/solvers/style3d/collision/collision.py#L203)) rather than an allocation size, so the same world scaling applies there with a different (untested by me) failure mode.

**Downstream.** Found in Isaac Lab, which maps one env to one Newton world. For a soft-body Franka manipulation task, `SolverVBD` construction starts failing with the `ValueError` above somewhere around 700-770 envs (the exact threshold varies because the soft body's tetrahedralization is not deterministic across runs).

### Reproduction Script

```python
"""SolverVBD sizes its body-particle contact buffers with the dense cross-world product
model.shape_count * model.particle_count, ignoring model.world_count.
"""

import warp as wp

import newton
import newton.solvers


def build(world_count: int, shapes_per_world: int, soft_dim: int, device: str) -> newton.Model:
    """world_count copies of {shapes_per_world boxes + a soft_dim^3 grid}, one per world."""
    tpl = newton.ModelBuilder()
    for j in range(shapes_per_world):
        tpl.add_shape_box(
            -1,
            xform=wp.transform(wp.vec3(0.25 * j, 0.0, 0.5), wp.quat_identity()),
            hx=0.05,
            hy=0.05,
            hz=0.05,
        )
    tpl.add_soft_grid(
        pos=wp.vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        rot=wp.quat_identity(),
        vel=wp.vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        dim_x=soft_dim,
        dim_y=soft_dim,
        dim_z=soft_dim,
        cell_x=0.05,
        cell_y=0.05,
        cell_z=0.05,
        density=100.0,
        k_mu=1000.0,
        k_lambda=1000.0,
        k_damp=0.0,
    )
    tpl.color()  # SolverVBD requires particle coloring
    builder = newton.ModelBuilder()
    builder.replicate(tpl, world_count=world_count)
    return builder.finalize(device=device)


print(f"newton {newton.__version__}, warp {wp.__version__}\n")
print(f"{'worlds':>7}{'shapes':>8}{'particles':>11}{'VBD allocates':>16}{'pipeline needs':>16}{'ratio':>7}{'VBD bytes':>13}")
for n in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64):

    vbd = m.shape_count * m.particle_count
    cp = newton.CollisionPipeline(m, soft_contact_max=None).soft_contact_max
    print(f"{m.world_count:>7}{m.shape_count:>8}{m.particle_count:>11}{vbd:>16,}{cp:>16,}{vbd / cp:>7.1f}{16 * vbd:>13,}")

# Same model shape, scaled until shape_count * particle_count crosses 2**31.
m = build(184, 64, 9, "cpu")
vbd = m.shape_count * m.particle_count
cp = newton.CollisionPipeline(m, soft_contact_max=None).soft_contact_max
print(f"\nworlds={m.world_count}  shapes={m.shape_count:,}  particles={m.particle_count:,}")
print(f"SolverVBD wants {vbd:,} slots = {16 * vbd / 1e9:.2f} GB; pipeline capacity is {cp:,} = {16 * cp / 1e6:.1f} MB")
try:

except ValueError as e:

```

- Warp: 1.17.0.dev20260725

title: Fix nested generic dataclass deserialization (#464)
issue_title: Generic deserialization does not work when dataclass is passed in generic arg
gold_patch:
diff --git a/serde/compat.py b/serde/compat.py
index d87e7d19..1a09e9eb 100644
--- a/serde/compat.py
+++ b/serde/compat.py
@@ -1153,10 +1153,19 @@ def get_generic_arg(
     'str'
     >>> get_generic_arg(GenericFoo[int, str], ['T', 'U'], ['U'], 0).__name__
     'str'
+    >>> get_generic_arg(GenericFoo[int, str], ['T', 'U'], None, 0).__name__
+    'int'
     """
-    if not is_generic(typ) or maybe_generic_type_vars is None or variable_type_args is None:
+    if not is_generic(typ) or maybe_generic_type_vars is None:
         return typing.Any
 
+    if variable_type_args is None:
+        # No remapping was supplied by the caller (e.g. when deserializing directly
+        # into a subscripted generic such as ``Foo[Bar[int]]``). In that case the
+        # field's type var maps straight onto the class's own type vars, so fall back
+        # to the identity mapping instead of losing the argument. See issue #464.
+        variable_type_args = maybe_generic_type_vars

     args = get_args(typ)
 
     if len(args) != len(maybe_generic_type_vars):

diff --git a/tests/test_basics.py b/tests/test_basics.py
index 7d5a3c9a..443a7430 100644
--- a/tests/test_basics.py
+++ b/tests/test_basics.py
@@ -8,7 +8,9 @@
 from beartype.roar import BeartypeCallHintViolation
 from typing import (
     ClassVar,
+    Generic,
     Optional,
+    TypeVar,
     Any,
 )
 from collections import defaultdict
@@ -1549,3 +1551,33 @@ class Foo:
 
     assert serde.to_dict(foo) == foo_se
     assert serde.from_dict(Foo, foo_se) == foo_de
+
+
+def test_generic_with_generic_dataclass_arg() -> None:
+    # https://github.com/yukinarit/pyserde/issues/464
+    # Deserializing into a generic whose type argument is itself a generic
+    # dataclass (e.g. ``Foo[Bar[int]]``) used to leave the inner dataclass as a
+    # raw dict instead of reconstructing it.
+    T = TypeVar("T")
+
+    @serde.serde
+    class Bar(Generic[T]):
+        inner: T
+
+    @serde.serde

+

+    assert f2 == serde.json.from_json(Foo[Bar[int]], json)

+    # Nested more than one level deep also works.
+    f3 = Foo(Bar(Bar(10)))
+    assert f3 == serde.json.from_json(Foo[Bar[Bar[int]]], serde.json.to_json(f3))

problem_statement.title: Generic deserialization does not work when dataclass is passed in generic arg
problem_statement.body:
```python
from typing import Generic, TypeVar
from serde import serde Trailing whitespace
from serde.json import from_json , to_json

T = TypeVar("T")

@serde
class Bar(Generic[T]):
    inner: T

@serde
class Foo(Generic[T]):
    inner: T


# This works
f1 = Foo(10)
json = to_json(f1)
print(json)
print(from_json(Foo[int], json))  # Prints Foo(inner=10)

# This does not work
f2 = Foo(Bar(10))
json = to_json(f2)
print(json)

# Foo(inner=Bar(inner=10)) is expected but prints Foo(inner={'inner': 10})
print(from_json(Foo[Bar[int]], json))
```

+# or a server that lost the lease to a peer would start refusing calls the lease

+# a capability boundary rather than a lock: it exists so a shared server can
+# serve recall to a client that must not change server state.

problem_statement.title: MCP --read-only gates on the palace-write set, so mempalace_hook_settings still rewrites config.json
problem_statement.body:
## What happened?

A server started with `--read-only` (or `MEMPALACE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1`) still advertises `mempalace_hook_settings` in `tools/list` and executes it, rewriting `~/.mempalace/config.json` on the server host.

Both halves of the gate test one set. `_mcp_read_only_refusal` (`mcp_server.py:4683`) and the `tools/list` filter (`:4764`) check `_MUTATING_TOOLS` (`:386-403`). That set exists for the peer-writer lease: `_mcp_peer_writer_refusal` (`:475-496`) uses it to decide which calls need the palace mine lock. `mempalace_hook_settings` touches no palace state, so it is rightly absent from it, but it does write, through `MempalaceConfig.set_hook_setting` (`config.py:1010-1019`). `service.WRITE_TOOLS` already lists the tool as a write, so the daemon's allowlist and the read-only gate disagree about it.

`mempalace_memories_filed_away` is the same shape: no palace state, but it unlinks `~/.mempalace/hook_state/last_checkpoint` (`:3741`, `:3750`).

#1930 fixed this class once, for `checkpoint` and `delete_by_source`. One line each worked there because both are palace writes, so the lease wanted them too. Neither tool above is a palace write, so the same move would put them under the palace lease, and a server that lost the lease to a peer would start refusing calls the lease has no say over.

## What did you expect?

A read-only server to refuse every tool that changes state on the server host, as `--read-only` promises: "Expose recall only: mutating tools are hidden and refused".

## How to reproduce

1. Start a read-only server against a palace whose `~/.mempalace/config.json` has `"desktop_toast": false`:

   ```bash
   mempalace serve --read-only --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765 &
   ```

2. Ask for the tool list. The tool is advertised, though it should be hidden:

   ```bash
   curl -s localhost:8765/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}' | grep -c mempalace_hook_settings
   ```

   ```
   1          expected 0
   ```

3. Call it. It succeeds instead of returning `-32003`:

   ```bash
   curl -s localhost:8765/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mempalace_hook_settings","arguments":{"desktop_toast":true}}}'
   ```

   ```
   "success": true, "updated": ["desktop_toast → True"]
   ```

4. The file on disk has changed:

   ```bash
   cat ~/.mempalace/config.json
   ```

   ```
   "desktop_toast": true
   ```

Same over stdio (`mempalace-mcp --read-only`) and with the environment variable instead of the flag.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 (kernel 6.18)
- Python version: 3.12.3
- MemPal version: develop `aa89bd82` (v3.6.0)

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 The Newton Developers
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Safely remove a temporary Newton release-audit report."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import re
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_REPORT_NAME = re.compile(r"newton-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.+-]*-(?:prerelease|rc|retrospective)-report\.md")
+
+
+def cleanup_report(path: Path, *, temporary_directory: Path | None = None) -> None:
+    """Remove an allowed report directly beneath the temporary directory."""
+    temporary_root = (temporary_directory or Path(tempfile.gettempdir())).resolve()
+    if path.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError("report path must not be a symlink")
+    candidate = path.resolve()
+    if candidate.parent != temporary_root:
+        raise ValueError(f"report must be directly beneath {temporary_root}")
+    if _REPORT_NAME.fullmatch(candidate.name) is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"not an allowed Newton report filename: {candidate.name}")
+    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Run the report cleanup command."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("path", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    try:
+        cleanup_report(args.path)
+    except ValueError as error:
+        parser.error(str(error))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Changelog fragments
+
+Pull requests with user-facing changes add changelog fragments instead of
+editing `CHANGELOG.md`. Towncrier combines the fragments on a release branch.
+
+## Choose an identifier
+
+Use a GitHub issue number when the work has an issue:
+
+```text
+3607.added.md
+3607.fixed.md
+```
+
+The number identifies an issue, not the pull request. This lets a developer or
+agent create the fragment before opening the pull request.
+
+When there is no issue, use a readable orphan identifier with a short random
+suffix:
+
+```text
++camera-rays-a1b2c3d4.added.md
+```
+
+The leading `+` tells Towncrier not to create a GitHub link. Use the same
+logical identifier for related entries when practical.
+
+## Choose categories and entries
+
+The supported categories, in rendered order, are:
+
+1. `added`
+2. `changed`
+3. `deprecated`
+4. `removed`
+5. `fixed`
+
+Towncrier treats each file as one entry and adds the Markdown bullet itself.
+Write imperative present tense, end the entry with a period, and do not start
+it with a hyphen followed by a space. Multiline entries and nested lists are
+supported:
+
+```markdown
+Add camera ray helpers with:
+
+  - Pinhole support.
+  - Fisheye support.
+```
+
+Use one file per entry. Add a numeric counter when one pull request has several
+entries in the same category:
+
+```text
+3607.added.md
+3607.added.1.md
+3607.deprecated.md
+3607.deprecated.1.md
+```
+
+For `changed`, `deprecated`, and `removed`, include migration guidance in the
+entry, such as: “Deprecate `Model.geo_meshes` in favor of `Model.shapes`.”
+
+If a pull request has no user-facing change, it may add a `.skip` file to record
+a one-line reason:
+
+```text
++camera-tests-a1b2c3d4.skip
+```
+
+Towncrier ignores `.skip` files. They are optional and do not affect the
+rendered changelog.
+
+## Create and preview
+
+Towncrier can create an issue-linked fragment:
+
+```console
+uvx --from towncrier==25.8.0 towncrier create 3607.added.md \
+  --content "Add camera ray helpers."
+```
+
+For an orphan, supply the readable random identifier directly. Towncrier's
+shorter `+.added.md` form also works, but generates an opaque random name.
+
+Preview the rendered output without modifying `CHANGELOG.md` or deleting
+fragments:
+
+```console
+uvx --from towncrier==25.8.0 towncrier build --draft \
+  --version X.Y.Z --date YYYY-MM-DD
+```
+
+`--draft` is the safe command to run during development. CI runs the same
+preview to confirm that Towncrier can render the current fragment set.
+
+## Assemble and maintain a release
+
+Build only on `release-X.Y`. After the initial release scope audit, assemble the
+current fragments early during RC stabilization. First render and approve the
+non-mutating preview, then run the mutating build:
+
+```console
+uvx --from towncrier==25.8.0 towncrier build --draft \
+  --version X.Y.Z --date YYYY-MM-DD
+uvx --from towncrier==25.8.0 towncrier build --yes \
+  --version X.Y.Z --date YYYY-MM-DD
+git rm --ignore-unmatch "changelog/*.skip"
+git add -A CHANGELOG.md changelog
+```

+rendered `.md` fragments. It ignores `.skip` files, so the release commit
+deletes those explicitly. Review the staged diff before committing.
+
+The first Towncrier release is a one-time transition. The insertion marker is
+already above the legacy `[Unreleased]` categories, so the old entries remain
+under the first generated release title. During that release audit, merge any
+duplicate category headings and verify that every legacy entry is retained.

+`release-management` label. Run the `release-changelog` cleanup against the
+assembled section for completeness, grouping, deduplication, wording,
+categories, and migration guidance.
+
+If more changes are cherry-picked before tagging, render only their fragments
+with `--draft`, fold the previewed entries into the existing dated section,
+delete exactly those `.md` and `.skip` fragments, and rerun the changelog and
+release audits. Final GA preparation verifies the completed section and that no
+release fragments remain.
+
+After the release, cherry-pick every changelog-management commit in order onto
+a changelog-only branch from `main`: the initial build, editorial cleanup, and
+later fragment additions. Open another `release-management` pull request. Git
+removes only fragments that shipped; fragments added to `main` after the
+release branch was cut remain pending for the next release.

problem_statement.title: Use changelog deltas
problem_statement.body:
When a PR has a merge conflict in most cases it is because of the CHANGELOG.md changes that GitHub is unable to merge because it doesn't follow the `merge=union` rule. This currently requires us to have the PR author fix the trivial merge conflict so the maintainer can merge the PR (if the maintainer fixed the conflict, they couldn't merge the PR even after they approved it because they made the last commit).

Isaac Lab is using a changelog deltas compilation script that works well for them, we should investigate something similar using a library such as [towncrier](https://pypi.org/project/towncrier/) or develop our own solution.

problem_statement.title: Workspace members are always treated as default dependencies
problem_statement.body:
### Describe the bug

Any workspace dependency added to the project as an optional or development dependency is marked as residing in `default` group in `pdm.lock` file.

### To reproduce

Clone repo: https://github.com/DenisKuplyakov/pdm-issue-3816 and run `./reproduce.sh`.

### Expected Behavior

Workspace projects are treated according to the dependency groups they are reside in as dependencies.

### Environment Information

```
PDM version:
  2.28.0
Python Interpreter:
  <REDACTED>/__2026-07-16-pdm-bug/.venv/bin/python (3.13)
Project Root:
  <REDACTED>/__2026-07-16-pdm-bug
Local Packages:
  <REDACTED>/__2026-07-16-pdm-bug/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages
{
  "implementation_name": "cpython",
  "implementation_version": "3.13.3",
  "os_name": "posix",
  "platform_machine": "x86_64",
  "platform_release": "6.15.0-1-default",
  "platform_system": "Linux",
  "platform_version": "#1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon Jun  2 07:13:45 UTC 2025 (17ba886)",
  "python_full_version": "3.13.3",
  "platform_python_implementation": "CPython",
  "python_version": "3.13",
  "sys_platform": "linux"
}
```

### Verbose Command Output

_No response_

### Additional Context

Removal of `[tool.pdm.workspace]` results in correct dependency groups handling. See https://github.com/DenisKuplyakov/pdm-issue-3816/commit/ee12697940729e25bee60fd7a1acb1569a4adeb7 in the reproducer.

### Are you willing to submit a PR to fix this bug?

- [ ] Yes, I would like to submit a PR.

+- Fixed `LLMFullResponseEndFrame` being silently dropped for every turn after the first when two turns' audio contexts were in flight concurrently. The end frame is now looked up per audio context instead of being gated by a single shared "response started" flag, which only ever fired for whichever turn's audio happened to finish first.

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelog/5108.fixed.md
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+- Fixed `LLMFullResponseStartFrame`/`LLMFullResponseEndFrame` arriving out of order at downstream processors (e.g. `LLMAssistantAggregator`) when a new LLM turn started while the previous turn's audio was still playing — reachable on TTS services that don't pause frame processing during synthesis (e.g. `CartesiaTTSService`), where a second, overlapping turn is possible. `LLMFullResponseStartFrame` is now routed through the same serialization queue as the rest of a turn's frames, so it can no longer be pushed ahead of an earlier turn's still-draining audio context.

+            # after any earlier audio context already queued has fully drained,
+            # rather than racing ahead of it (e.g. a new turn starting via
+            # LLMMessagesAppendFrame while the previous turn's audio is still
+            # playing out downstream).
+            await self._serialization_queue.put(frame)
         elif isinstance(frame, (LLMFullResponseEndFrame, EndFrame)):

         when the context queue is drained). Resets the PTS baseline so the next turn
-        starts fresh. If an LLM response is still marked as in-progress and text frames
-        are not being pushed (which would have already emitted the frame), the end

problem_statement.title: LLMAssistantAggregator merges overlapping LLM response cycles into one corrupted assistant message
problem_statement.body:
### Pipecat version

1.2.0 (also present on `main` and `v1.3.0` — see note below)

### Python version

3.12.12

### Operating System

Linux

### Issue description

`LLMAssistantAggregator` accumulates streamed assistant text in a single `_aggregation` buffer. That buffer is only cleared by `push_aggregation()` (on `LLMFullResponseEndFrame`) and by `_handle_interruptions()`. The turn-start path does **not** clear it:

```python
async def _handle_llm_start(self, _: LLMFullResponseStartFrame):
    await self._trigger_assistant_turn_started()

async def _trigger_assistant_turn_started(self):
    self._assistant_turn_start_timestamp = time_now_iso8601()   # no reset of _aggregation
    await self._call_event_handler("on_assistant_turn_started")
```

As a result, if a **second** `LLMFullResponseStartFrame` arrives while a turn is still open (buffer non-empty, and no `LLMFullResponseEndFrame`/interruption flushed it in between), the new cycle's `TextFrame`s are appended on top of the previous cycle's leftover. The two cycles are then committed to the context as **one merged, corrupted assistant message** — doubled prefixes and run-together words.

This is not a hypothetical: it happens in production when a second generation for the same turn is triggered before the first is flushed. In our case an idle/presence check issued via `LLMMessagesAppendFrame(run_llm=True)` (which pushes a context frame upstream and starts a generation) raced the user's reply, which started its own generation. The committed assistant message came out as e.g.:

```
[say lightly with [[say lightly with a friendly, conversational tone]say  Greatlightly,  with thanks. Just to confirm, ...
```

(We use Inworld TTS audio-tag prompting, so each line is prefixed with a `[say ... tone]` tag — hence the doubled `[[say ...]` and the mashed `Greatlightly`.)

`_handle_interruptions()` already does the right thing (`_trigger_assistant_turn_stopped(interrupted=True)` + `reset()`); the gap is that a new turn start does not get the same treatment.

### Reproduction steps

Minimal, no LLM / no transport — drives the aggregator's frame handlers directly to isolate the buffer behavior:

```python
import asyncio
from pipecat.processors.aggregators.llm_context import LLMContext
from pipecat.processors.aggregators.llm_response_universal import LLMContextAggregatorPair
from pipecat.frames.frames import (
    LLMFullResponseStartFrame, LLMFullResponseEndFrame, LLMTextFrame,
)

async def main():
    assistant = LLMContextAggregatorPair(context=LLMContext()).assistant()

    # Cycle A starts and streams some text...
    await assistant._handle_llm_start(LLMFullResponseStartFrame())
    await assistant._handle_text(LLMTextFrame("[tag] Great"))

    # Cycle B starts before A was flushed by an end frame / interruption.
    await assistant._handle_llm_start(LLMFullResponseStartFrame())
    await assistant._handle_text(LLMTextFrame("[tag] thanks, just to confirm."))
    await assistant._handle_llm_end(LLMFullResponseEndFrame())

    for m in assistant._context.get_messages():
        print(m)

asyncio.run(main())
```

Output:

```
{'role': 'assistant', 'content': '[tag] Great[tag] thanks, just to confirm.'}
```

In the wild the second cycle is started by a real frame (e.g. `LLMMessagesAppendFrame(run_llm=True)`) racing a user turn, rather than by calling the handler directly — but the merge mechanism is the same.

### Expected behavior

A new `LLMFullResponseStartFrame` arriving while a turn is still open should close/flush the stale turn first (the same way an interruption does), so the two response cycles surface as **two separate assistant messages**:

```
{'role': 'assistant', 'content': '[tag] Great'}
{'role': 'assistant', 'content': '[tag] thanks, just to confirm.'}
```

### Actual behavior

The two cycles are concatenated into a single corrupted assistant message (`'[tag] Great[tag] thanks, just to confirm.'`), which is then committed to the context and surfaced via `on_assistant_turn_stopped`.

### Logs

Note: still present on `main` and `v1.3.0` — `_trigger_assistant_turn_started()` does not reset `_aggregation` on either, and the non-realtime `_handle_llm_start` path is unchanged. A local workaround we use is to subclass the assistant aggregator and, in `_handle_llm_start`, flush+reset (`_trigger_assistant_turn_stopped(interrupted=True)` then `reset()`) when `self._assistant_turn_start_timestamp` is set and `self._aggregation` is non-empty, before delegating to `super()`.

+transition; a finished (or non-cron) row must not. Because cron session ids

+    # / regex literals and comments (same hardened extractor as the sibling #5744

+    body = r"""
+function extractFunc(name) {
+  const re = new RegExp('function\\s+' + name + '\\s*\\(');
+  const start = src.search(re);
+  if (start < 0) throw new Error(name + ' not found');
+  let i = src.indexOf('{', start);
+  let depth = 1; i++;
+  let str = null;
+  let inLine = false;
+  let inBlock = false;
+  let inRegex = false;
+  let prev = '';
+  while (depth > 0 && i < src.length) {
+    const c = src[i];
+    const n = src[i + 1];
+    if (inLine) { if (c === '\n') inLine = false; i++; continue; }

+      if (c === '/') inRegex = false;

+    if (c === '/' && n === '*') { inBlock = true; i += 2; continue; }

+    # to the shorter cron_backup_ prefix (it belongs to a completed run).
+    assert by_sid["cron_backup_full_20260803_190000"]["cron_running"] is False

+    # Single running job, non-overlapping id: unchanged behavior.

+    )
+    assert rows[0]["cron_running"] is True

+def test_overlay_shorter_running_job_cannot_claim_longer_job_session(monkeypatch):
+    """A running `backup` must NOT claim a `backup_full` session when only
+
+    `backup` is running (#6728 gate finding). Prefixes are built ONLY from
+    RUNNING jobs, so if `backup_full` is not running, longest-prefix sorting
+    never sees the true longer owner and `cron_backup_` would otherwise swallow
+    `cron_backup_full_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`. The remainder after the matched prefix
+    must be EXACTLY a run timestamp, so `full_20260803_210000` is rejected.
+    """
+    import api.routes as routes
+    import api.route_session_list_cache as slc
+
+    # Only `backup` is running; `backup_full` is NOT tracked.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(routes, "_RUNNING_CRON_JOBS", {"backup": 1000.0})

+    assert by_sid["cron_backup_20260803_100000"]["cron_running"] is True
+    # The `backup_full` session must stay completed — `backup`'s prefix leaves
+    # `full_20260803_210000`, which is not a bare run timestamp.
+    assert by_sid["cron_backup_full_20260803_210000"]["cron_running"] is False

+
+def test_running_cron_row_renders_effectively_streaming():
+    """A row with cron_running=true must render ACTIVE in the sidebar.
+
+    Rendering, sorting, polling and completion-transition tracking all key off
+    `_isSessionEffectivelyStreaming` (static/sessions.js). Before the fix the
+    predicate ignored `cron_running`, so a running cron row rendered visually
+    idle and could lose its eventual completion/unread transition.
+    """
+    js = SESSIONS_JS_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    source = _extract_func_script(js) + _js_prelude() + r"""
+eval(extractFunc('_hasPendingUserMessageSignal'));
+eval(extractFunc('_isSessionLocallyStreaming'));

+
+
+def test_cron_running_defers_completion_unread_until_flag_clears():
+    """A cron_running row with advanced message_count must NOT be marked
+    completed-unread; exactly ONE true->false completion transition happens
+    when the flag clears.
+
+    The `!cronRunning` guards in `_markPollingCompletionUnreadTransitions`
+    defer all three completion signals while the job runs; the focused
+    regression proves the row is only marked once, on the poll where
+    cron_running flips to false.
+    """
+    js = SESSIONS_JS_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    source = _extract_func_script(js) + _js_prelude() + r"""
+eval(extractFunc('_hasPendingUserMessageSignal'));
+eval(extractFunc('_isSessionLocallyStreaming'));
+eval(extractFunc('_isSessionEffectivelyStreaming'));
+eval(extractFunc('_markPollingCompletionUnreadTransitions'));
+const sid = 'cron_job6728_20260803_100000';
+_sessionListSnapshotById.set(sid, { message_count: 1, last_message_at: 1000 });
+let row = {
+  session_id: sid,
+  cron_running: true,
+  is_streaming: false,
+  message_count: 2,
+  last_message_at: 1100,
+};
+// Poll 1: cron still running, message_count advanced -> no completion mark.
+_markPollingCompletionUnreadTransitions([row]);
+const marksWhileRunning = markCount;
+const streamWhileRunning = _sessionStreamingById.get(sid);
+// Poll 2: cron flag clears -> exactly one true->false completion transition.
+row.cron_running = false;
+_markPollingCompletionUnreadTransitions([row]);
+const marksAfterClear = markCount;
+const streamAfterClear = _sessionStreamingById.get(sid);
+console.log(JSON.stringify({
+  marksWhileRunning,
+  marksAfterClear,
+  streamWhileRunning,
+  streamAfterClear,
+  markedSids,
+}));
+"""
+    m = json.loads(_run_node(source))
+    assert m["marksWhileRunning"] == 0, (
+        "cron_running row with advanced message_count must not be marked completed-unread"
+    )
+    assert m["marksAfterClear"] == 1, "exactly one completion transition when the flag clears"
+    assert m["streamWhileRunning"] is True, "row must render active while cron_running"
+    assert m["streamAfterClear"] is False
+    assert m["markedSids"] == ["cron_job6728_20260803_100000"]

problem_statement.title: bug(cron): active cron sessions wrongly appear as completed in sidebar
problem_statement.body:
**Bug:** an active (still-running) cron job's session is painted as *completed* in the sidebar the moment it appends a new message, before the job actually finishes.

### Repro
1. Trigger a cron job that runs for a while (scheduled or via `/api/crons/run`).
2. Watch its session row in the sidebar while the job is mid-run.
3. As soon as a new message lands, the row picks up a completion/unread dot.

**Expected:** the row shows an active/running indicator while the job executes and flips to completed only when the job ends.

## Root cause (split-brain between two server state sources the sidebar never reconciles)
- Cron liveness lives only in the in-memory `_RUNNING_CRON_JOBS` dict — `api/routes.py:1328-1344` (`_mark_cron_running` / `_mark_cron_done` / `_is_cron_running`) — and is surfaced **only** via `/api/crons/status` (`_handle_cron_status`, `api/routes.py:20345`).
- The sidebar polls **only** `/api/sessions`, deriving "running" from session-row fields via `_isSessionEffectivelyStreaming` (`static/sessions.js:814`). Cron rows never get `is_streaming=True`, so the completion heuristic in `_markPollingCompletionUnreadTransitions` (`static/sessions.js:1188`) trips `completedWithNewMessages` (line 1217) on every mid-run message.
- The existing cron guard (lines 1236-1247) filters only by **profile**, never by whether the job is still running.

## Suggested fix
- **Server:** in `_build_session_list_cache_payload` (`api/routes.py:2159`), mark cron rows whose `session_id` matches `_is_cron_running` with `is_streaming`/`cron_running`.
- **Client:** `_markPollingCompletionUnreadTransitions` should skip/defer "completed" for cron-source rows while the job runs (honor the flag or gate on real job completion).

## Related
- `tests/test_issue4385_cron_archive_reappears.py` (cron row identity contract — must not stamp cron as CLI).
- Present on `upstream/master` `320789ae` (2026-07-31); verified code path, not yet live-repro'd.

problem_statement.title: raise CloseSpider("Error Message") is not saving error message
problem_statement.body:
When I run the code `raise CloseSpider("Error Message")` in the Spider **parse** function, the reason gets saved in the **finish_reason** stats string.

When it is run in the **start_requests** function, the spider properly closes but the **finish_reason** does not have the message it in.  The finish_reason value is "finished" instead of "Error Message" as set in the CloseSpider exception.

Is this intentional or a bug?  thanks!

problem_statement.title: QueryExpander returns duplicate generated queries
problem_statement.body:
**Describe the bug**

`QueryExpander` can return duplicate queries when the chat generator repeats an expansion. It only checks whether the original query is already present; duplicates among the generated expansions are preserved.

This is especially visible when the component feeds `MultiQueryTextRetriever` or `MultiQueryEmbeddingRetriever`: each duplicate entry triggers another retrieval for the same query, adding latency and backend load while reducing the effective number of distinct expansions.

I reproduced this on the current `main` commit `bfb7a2896a393f031ccc7669b6923a32ca27918d`.

**Error message**

No exception is raised. The output contains duplicate query strings:

```text
{'queries': ['same query', 'same query', 'other query']}
```

**Expected behavior**

The output should contain each generated query once while preserving first-seen order. The original query should also appear at most once when `include_original_query=True`.

For the reproduction below, the expected result is:

```text
{'queries': ['same query', 'other query']}
```

**Additional context**

The sync and async paths contain the same post-processing logic, so both are affected. The existing `test_run_query_deduplication` test only covers a generated expansion matching the original query, not duplicates among generated expansions.

I searched existing open and closed issues and pull requests for `QueryExpander`, `duplicate query`, and `query expansion duplicates` and did not find a report or implementation covering this case.

If the maintainers confirm this behavior should be fixed and mark it open for external contribution, I would be happy to add an order-preserving regression fix for both sync and async execution paths.

**To Reproduce**

```python
import json

from haystack.components.generators.chat import MockChatGenerator
from haystack.components.query import QueryExpander

payload = json.dumps(
    {"queries": ["same query", "same query", "other query"]}
)
expander = QueryExpander(
    chat_generator=MockChatGenerator(payload),
    n_expansions=3,
    include_original_query=False,
)

print(expander.run("topic"))
```

Run with:

```console
hatch -e test run python reproduce.py
```

The same duplicate list is returned by `await expander.run_async("topic")`.

**FAQ Check**
- [x] Have you had a look at [our new FAQ page](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/faq)?

**System:**
- OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (build 26200)
- Python: 3.13.12
- Haystack version: `main` at `bfb7a2896a393f031ccc7669b6923a32ca27918d`

problem_statement.title: Support `REPLACE USING` for INSERT
problem_statement.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I am trying to parse a Databricks SQL as such
```
import sqlglot

# https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-dml-insert-into#replace-using
sql = """
INSERT INTO TABLE students
    REPLACE USING (country)
    SELECT * FROM new_students;
"""
sqlglot.parse_one(sql, dialect="databricks"
```

But currently the core parser/generator does not handle such case, and are impossible to be overridden at dialect level.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I would like the core parser/generator to support this `REPLACE USING` expression.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I think the most fundamental solution is change `where` in [dml.Insert](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/blob/33de21fc21cdc05755a2de39318b292c10ccec0f/sqlglot/expressions/dml.py#L195) to something more general, like `replace`, and implement a method `parse_insert_replace` in the core parser, in this way, each dialect can implement their own "insert replace" parsing/generation.
But this solution introduces a breaking change.

I am new to sqlglot so just came up with the two solutions. Would like to hear some feedback from the team.

**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

problem_statement.title: BUG: Censored discrete distributions with integer bounds fail logprob derivation since 6.2.0 (find_measurable_clips builds a type-mismatched replacement)
problem_statement.body:
## Description

Since 6.2.0, `pm.Censored` over a **discrete** distribution fails logprob derivation whenever the bounds or observed values are integers — which is the natural dtype for them. Continuous distributions are unaffected. Bisects to the censoring rework in #8363 (merged 2026-07-19, released in 6.2.0); still present on current `main`.

The failure is effectively unavoidable from the user side: passing integer observations doesn't help, because pymc's own observed-data handling converts them to float64, which the rewrite then rejects against the integer graph. The only working form is casting **both** `upper` and `observed` to float yourself, which a user has no way to discover.

```python
import numpy as np
import pymc as pm

with pm.Model() as m:
    pm.Censored("y", pm.Poisson.dist(3), lower=None, upper=np.full(10, 5), observed=np.full(10, 3))
    m.logp()
# RuntimeError: The logprob terms of the following value variables could not be derived: ...
```

With `pytensor.config.exception_verbosity` raised, the underlying rewrite failure is visible:

```
<<!! BUG IN FGRAPH.REPLACE OR A LISTENER !!>> <class 'TypeError'>
Cannot convert Type Vector(int64, shape=(10,)) (of Variable MeasurableClip.0)
into Type Vector(float64, shape=(10,)). ... find_measurable_clips
```

Behavior matrix on 6.2.0 (all pass on 6.0.x):

| case | result |
|---|---|
| Censored **continuous** (Normal), any dtype mix | OK |
| Censored **discrete** (Poisson), float upper & observed | OK |
| Censored **discrete** (Poisson), integer upper and/or observed | **RuntimeError** |

## Cause

A dtype disagreement between the node built by `pm.Censored` and the replacement built by `find_measurable_clips`:

1. `Censored` with `lower=None` compiles to `clip(rv, -inf, upper)`. The float `-inf` promotes the **original Clip node to float64** even for an int64 base RV, and the value variable is created to match (float64).
2. The reworked `find_measurable_clips` deliberately uses the base variable as the unbounded sentinel — the comment says *"unlike +-inf constants, it does not upcast discrete variables"* — so the **replacement `MeasurableClip` comes out int64**.
3. `fgraph.replace` correctly refuses the float64 → int64 substitution, the rewrite dies, no measurable node exists, and `conditional_logp` raises the generic `RuntimeError`.

Neither half is wrong in isolation; the replacement just isn't type-preserving against the node it replaces.

## Proposed fix

Reuse #8363's own idiom (emit the explicit op, let the existing rewrite claim it on a later pass), applied to promoted clips — when the measurable clip's dtype differs from the original node's, relabel it with an explicit widening cast and let `find_measurable_casts` claim it as measure-preserving:

```diff
     clipped_rv = (
         MeasurableClip(scalar_clip).make_node(base_var, lower_bound, upper_bound).outputs[0]
     )
+
+    [old_out] = node.outputs
+    if clipped_rv.type.dtype != old_out.type.dtype:
+        # The +-inf sentinel in the original graph upcast a discrete base; the
+        # measurable clip preserves the base dtype instead, so relabel it with an
+        # explicit cast and let find_measurable_casts claim the widening cast as
+        # measure-preserving on a later pass.
+        clipped_rv = pt.cast(clipped_rv, old_out.type.dtype)
+
     return [clipped_rv]
```

## Verification of the fix

Applied to 6.2.0 and compared against a pymc 6.0.1 reference environment — **bit-identical logp on every probe**, including edge cases:

- interior observation: exactly `n * poisson.logpmf(3, 3)`; observation at the censor point: exactly the survival mass `n * log P(X >= 5)`
- non-integral observed below the bound and at a non-integral censor point: identical to 6.0.1 (pymc's discrete logps evaluate the formula without integrality checks — pre-existing behavior, unchanged by this fix)
- latent (unobserved) censored discrete variable: identical
- partially `-inf` lower-bound vector: identical (that path keeps a float bound and never fires the new branch)
- censored continuous distributions: unaffected (dtypes already agree)

Not exercised: the clip-of-clip fusion branch on `main` (the patch compares against `node.outputs[0]`, so it should compose, but a test would be good) and `floatX="float32"`.

Happy to open a PR with the patch plus regression tests if the approach looks right.

## Context

Found while bumping pymc-marketing to pymc 6.2 (pymc-labs/pymc-marketing#2803): our `ShiftedBetaGeoModel` is a `Censored(ShiftedBetaGeometric, upper=T)` with integer `T` — every test of that model broke. Downstream we work around it by casting `upper`/`observed` to float, which behaves identically on 6.0/6.2/main.

## Versions

- pymc 6.2.0 (also reproduced on main @ `9e94b48`)
- pytensor 3.2.4, numpy 2.4.6, python 3.13, macOS/Linux

problem_statement.title: Failure to read HDF5 data with data arrays of dtype='<U1'
problem_statement.body:
Hello,
I am exploring VirtualiZarr/IceChunk for our workflow. I followed VirtualiZarr's example of reading one of our NetCDF files into VirtualiZarr:

```
import obstore
import virtualizarr as vz
from virtualizarr.parsers import HDFParser
from obspec_utils.registry import ObjectStoreRegistry

bucket = 's3://its-live-data'
granule = "velocity_image_pair/landsatOLI/v02/S80W170/LC08_L1GT_020121_20231013_20231102_02_T2_X_LC09_L1GT_020121_20231106_20231106_02_T2_G0120V02_P084.nc"

store = obstore.store.from_url(bucket, region="us-west-2", skip_signature=True)
registry = ObjectStoreRegistry({bucket: store})
parser = HDFParser()
# parser = HDFParser(drop_variables=['img_pair_info', 'mapping'])

vds = vz.open_virtual_dataset(
    url=f"{bucket}/{granule}",
    parser=parser,
    registry=registry,
    loadable_variables=[],
    
)
```

I'm getting the following failure:
```
virtualizarr/parsers/hdf/hdf.py:82
fill_value = dataset.fillvalue.item()
AttributeError: 'bytes' object has no attribute 'item'
```
It appears to be linked to the data variables of `string` dtype that don't have` _FillValue `attribute specified. Thinking it's a `_FillValue` issue, I added `_FillValue` attribute to our data and it failed with:

```
File [.../lib/python3.13/site-packages/xarray/backends/zarr.py:141](http://localhost:8888/...lib/python3.13/site-packages/xarray/backends/zarr.py#line=140), in FillValueCoder.encode(cls, value, dtype)
    139     return str(value)
    140 else:
--> 141     raise ValueError(f"Failed to encode fill_value. Unsupported dtype {dtype}")

ValueError: Failed to encode fill_value. Unsupported dtype object
```

Is it a bug or I'm doing something wrong?

If I exclude two "trouble" variables of string type (`parser = HDFParser(drop_variables=['img_pair_info', 'mapping'])`) when loading the data, the code works. 

After realizing that even if we get `img_pair_info` data read into the virtual dataset, we would not be able to preserve the attribute values we are interested in during the merge of all datasets into the virtual cube.
Is there a way to serialize data variable attributes into new variables of the virtual datacube when loading the data?I realize it can be done manually if `img_pair_info` is loaded into the virtual dataset — by extracting the attribute values and adding them as new data variables to the virtual dataset after calling `vz.open_virtual_dataset()`.

Is there a way to load the `mapping` into the datasets, but not to merge it as it's kind of a "constant" value that applies to all layers of the datacube?

I am using 
obstore 0.8.2
virtualizarr 2.4.0

Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,
Masha

+"""Stopgap drift guard: the frontend ``_MSG_LIMIT_MAX`` mirror must match the
+backend ``_MAX_MSG_LIMIT`` ceiling.
+
+PR #6152 introduced the server-side ``_MAX_MSG_LIMIT`` ceiling on
+``GET /api/session ?msg_limit=``. PR #6154 added a hand-mirrored
+``_MSG_LIMIT_MAX`` in ``static/sessions.js`` so the frontend knows when to
+switch from the growing-tail strategy to ``msg_before`` paging. If the two
+drift, load-older silently stalls at the old value — the exact regression #6154
+fixed. The durable fix (#6177) exposes the ceiling via ``/api/session`` metadata
+so the mirror isn't needed; until then, this static-source assertion catches the
+drift.
+
+Placement note: this test ships in #6152 (where ``_MAX_MSG_LIMIT`` is defined).
+The frontend ``_MSG_LIMIT_MAX`` only exists once #6154 lands, so the assertion
+SKIPS when the JS constant is absent — it activates automatically once both
+branches are on master, and bites if the two values ever diverge.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+
+
+def _backend_max_msg_limit() -> int:
+    """Extract ``_MAX_MSG_LIMIT = <int>`` from api/routes.py."""
+    src = (ROOT / "api" / "routes.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    m = re.search(r"^_MAX_MSG_LIMIT\s*=\s*(\d+)\s*$", src, re.MULTILINE)
+    assert m, "_MAX_MSG_LIMIT not found in api/routes.py"
+    return int(m.group(1))
+
+
+def _frontend_msg_limit_max():
+    """Extract ``_MSG_LIMIT_MAX = <int>`` from static/sessions.js, or return
+    None when the constant is absent (PR #6154 not yet landed)."""
+    sessions = ROOT / "static" / "sessions.js"
+    if not sessions.exists():
+        return None
+    src = sessions.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    m = re.search(r"const\s+_MSG_LIMIT_MAX\s*=\s*(\d+)\s*;", src)
+    return int(m.group(1)) if m else None
+
+
+def test_frontend_msg_limit_max_matches_backend_ceiling():
+    """When both constants exist (i.e. #6152 + #6154 have both landed), the
+    frontend mirror MUST equal the backend ceiling or load-older silently stalls
+    for long sessions. Skips gracefully when the JS constant is absent (the
+    #6152-only state) so this test ships atomically with the backend constant
+    without depending on the #6154 branch."""
+    backend = _backend_max_msg_limit()
+    frontend = _frontend_msg_limit_max()
+    if frontend is None:
+        # PR #6154 (the frontend mirror) hasn't landed yet — skip rather than
+        # fail. Once both are on master this branch is exercised and bites on
+        # any drift.
+        import pytest
+        pytest.skip("_MSG_LIMIT_MAX not yet present in static/sessions.js "
+                    "(lands in #6154); drift guard activates once both are on master")
+    assert frontend == backend, (
+        f"frontend _MSG_LIMIT_MAX ({frontend}) != backend _MAX_MSG_LIMIT ({backend}): "
+        f"load-older will silently stall at the wrong value. Update both together, "
+        f"or land #6177 (metadata-exposure) to retire the mirror."
+    )
+
+
+def test_backend_max_msg_limit_is_reasonable():
+    """The backend ceiling must exist and stay in a sane range (the frontend's
+    real pagination grows by ~30, so anything in [100, 2000] is generous)."""
+    backend = _backend_max_msg_limit()
+    assert 100 <= backend <= 2000, f"_MAX_MSG_LIMIT out of expected range: {backend}"

@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+"""Tests: server-side ``msg_limit`` ceiling on ``GET /api/session``.
+
+A client could request ``msg_limit=1000000`` (or the frontend's
+``msg_limit=9999`` outline-jump path) and force the server to assemble and
+serialize an unbounded message payload. The handler now clamps ``msg_limit`` to
+``_MAX_MSG_LIMIT`` (generous — far above any legitimate visible-row window) so
+real pagination is unaffected while the pathological/oversized request is
+bounded. The existing ``_messages_truncated`` signal covers the clamped case.
+
+The parse+clamp lives in ``_parse_msg_limit`` so the clamping expression has
+direct test coverage (driving the handler end-to-end would require a live
+session + state.db; the helper is the unit under test).
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from api.routes import _MAX_MSG_LIMIT, _parse_msg_limit
+
+
+def test_max_msg_limit_constant_is_reasonable():
+    """The ceiling must exist and be well above legitimate pagination sizes
+    (the frontend grows windows by ~30, initial load is 30) but finite."""
+    assert isinstance(_MAX_MSG_LIMIT, int)
+    assert 100 <= _MAX_MSG_LIMIT <= 2000, _MAX_MSG_LIMIT
+
+
+def test_parse_msg_limit_none_when_absent_or_empty():
+    """No value (the bare no-msg_limit path) returns None — intentionally the
+    'full transcript' escape hatch for branch/undo/jump-to-start flows."""
+    assert _parse_msg_limit(None) is None
+    assert _parse_msg_limit("") is None
+
+
+def test_parse_msg_limit_none_when_malformed():
+    """A non-numeric value returns None rather than raising (matches the
+    pre-fix behavior where a ValueError fell through to msg_limit=None)."""
+    assert _parse_msg_limit("not-a-number") is None
+    assert _parse_msg_limit("abc") is None

+
+def test_parse_msg_limit_passes_legit_sizes_unchanged():
+    """Legitimate pagination sizes (5/30/60/100) are returned verbatim — the
+    ceiling only caps oversized requests."""
+    for legit in (1, 5, 30, 60, 100):
+        if legit > _MAX_MSG_LIMIT:
+            continue
+        assert _parse_msg_limit(str(legit)) == legit, f"legit {legit} altered"
+
+
+def test_parse_msg_limit_clamps_oversized_to_ceiling():
+    """An over-ceiling request (the outline-jump 9999, or a hostile 1000000) is
+    clamped down to _MAX_MSG_LIMIT — exactly the regression this PR fixes."""
+    assert _parse_msg_limit("9999") == _MAX_MSG_LIMIT
+    assert _parse_msg_limit("1000000") == _MAX_MSG_LIMIT
+    assert _parse_msg_limit(str(_MAX_MSG_LIMIT + 1)) == _MAX_MSG_LIMIT
+
+
+def test_parse_msg_limit_ceiling_boundary_itself_passes():
+    """A request exactly at the ceiling is allowed (clamp is inclusive)."""
+    assert _parse_msg_limit(str(_MAX_MSG_LIMIT)) == _MAX_MSG_LIMIT
+
+
+def test_parse_msg_limit_zero_and_negative_clamp_to_one():
+    """Non-positive values clamp to the minimum (1), not None — a caller asking
+    for msg_limit=0 gets a 1-row window, not the full transcript."""
+    assert _parse_msg_limit("0") == 1
+    assert _parse_msg_limit("-5") == 1

problem_statement.title: tech(contract): expose msg_limit ceiling in /api/session metadata so the frontend doesn't hand-mirror _MAX_MSG_LIMIT
problem_statement.body:
## Context

PR #6152 introduced a server-side ceiling on `GET /api/session ?msg_limit=` (`_MAX_MSG_LIMIT = 500`, `api/routes.py`). PR #6154 fixed the two frontend paths that relied on unbounded `msg_limit` (outline jump, endless scroll) and added a hand-mirrored `_MSG_LIMIT_MAX = 500` constant in `static/sessions.js` so the frontend knows when to switch from the growing-tail strategy to `msg_before` paging.

Both #6152 and #6154 reviewers (Greptile and maintainer) flagged the same fragility: **the two constants are coupled by hand with no automated guard.** If the backend ceiling changes and the frontend mirror isn't updated, load-older silently stalls again at the old value — the exact regression #6154 fixed — with no test to catch it.

## Proposal

Surface the ceiling in the `/api/session` response metadata (alongside the existing `_messages_offset` / `_messages_truncated` fields), e.g. a `_msg_limit_max` field, and have the frontend read it instead of hardcoding `_MSG_LIMIT_MAX`.

Rough shape:
- Backend (`api/routes.py`): add `raw["_msg_limit_max"] = _MAX_MSG_LIMIT` to the `GET /api/session` response (near where `_messages_truncated` is set, ~line 12708).
- Frontend (`static/sessions.js`): read `data.session._msg_limit_max` on load (default to the current `500` literal if absent for backward-compat with older servers), and use it as the threshold in `_loadOlderMessages`'s `useBeforePaging` check.
- Drop the hand-mirrored `_MSG_LIMIT_MAX` constant (or keep it only as the fallback default).

This removes the coupling entirely — the frontend always follows whatever the server's actual ceiling is.

## Why track separately

This spans both #6152 (backend) and #6154 (frontend) and changes a response contract field, so it shouldn't be silently folded into either. It's also strictly a hardening follow-up — #6154's mirror works correctly today; this just removes the maintenance footgun.

## Optional automated guard (until the metadata exposure lands)

Until the metadata field ships, a static-source assertion test could read both `api/routes.py` (`_MAX_MSG_LIMIT = <N>`) and `static/sessions.js` (`_MSG_LIMIT_MAX = <N>`) and fail if they differ. The repo already has a JS-source-reading test helper (`tests/js_source_extract.py`), so this is cheap. This is a stopgap; the metadata exposure above is the real fix.

## References

- #6152 — backend `msg_limit` ceiling
- #6154 — frontend follow-up (introduces the `_MSG_LIMIT_MAX` mirror this issue would retire)
- Maintainer comment on #6154 flagging the coupling

## Model Used

problem_statement.title: Python executor INTERSECT ALL and EXCEPT ALL discard multiplicity
problem_statement.body:
**Before you file an issue**

- The defect is reproduced on current `main` commit `33de21fc21cdc05755a2de39318b292c10ccec0f`.
- The relevant path is SQLGlot's dialect-independent Python executor, so separate read and write dialect settings do not apply.
- Refreshed open and closed issue, pull-request, source-history, and release searches found no exact duplicate.

**Fully reproducible code snippet**

```python
from sqlglot.executor import execute

left = [{"v": 1}, {"v": 1}, {"v": 1}]
right = [{"v": 1}, {"v": 1}]
tables = {"x": left, "y": right}
print(execute("SELECT v FROM x INTERSECT ALL SELECT v FROM y", tables=tables).rows)
print(execute("SELECT v FROM x EXCEPT ALL SELECT v FROM y", tables=tables).rows)
```

`INTERSECT ALL` returns one row instead of two, and `EXCEPT ALL` returns no rows instead of one. The corresponding DISTINCT forms are controls and correctly return set-like output.

**Expected behavior**

`ALL` operations must preserve multiset cardinality.

**Root cause**

`PythonExecutor.set_operation` converts both inputs to Python sets for `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT`, regardless of the planner's `distinct` flag.

**Proposed correction**

Use counted row consumption for `ALL` and stable first-occurrence set behavior for `DISTINCT`.

**Validation**

The isolated local correction has a positive regression, DISTINCT controls, and a passing 21-test executor suite. The validated correction is available in linked pull request #7955.

**Official documentation**

- SQLGlot optimizer and executor API: https://sqlglot.com/sqlglot.html
- Repository contribution guide: https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

test_patch:
diff --git a/console/src/pages/Chat/tests/sessionCacheStaleness.test.ts b/console/src/pages/Chat/tests/sessionCacheStaleness.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..c470de61a1f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/console/src/pages/Chat/tests/sessionCacheStaleness.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,118 @@
+/**
+ * Regression test for issue #6131 follow-up:
+ * "Messages sent from an external channel (DingTalk) don't appear in the
+ *  console conversation; switching away and back doesn't help — only a full
+ *  page refresh shows them."
+ *
+ * Root cause: SessionApi keeps an in-memory LRU cache of converted messages
+ * keyed by backend UUID. On session switch-back, `fetchAndBuildSession`
+ * returned the cached messages for idle chats WITHOUT re-fetching. The cache
+ * was only invalidated when the LOCAL user sent a message — never when a
+ * message arrived from an external channel. A full page refresh worked only
+ * because it recreates the SessionApi singleton (empty cache).
+ *
+ * Fix: the cache entry now records the chat's backend `updated_at`; on read we
+ * compare it against the freshly-polled `updated_at` from the session list and
+ * treat the entry as stale (re-fetch) when the backend is newer.
+ *
+ * These tests drive the public `getSession` / `getSessionList` flow with
+ * mocked `api.getChat` / `api.listChats`, asserting a re-fetch happens exactly
+ * when `updated_at` advances (and NOT when it stays the same).
+ */
+import { describe, it, expect, vi, afterEach } from "vitest";
+import type { ChatSpec, ChatHistory, Message } from "../../../api";
+import api from "../../../api";
+import sessionApi from "../sessionApi";
+
+const T0 = "2026-07-16T15:30:00.000000+00:00";
+const T1 = "2026-07-16T15:36:00.000000+00:00";
+
+function makeChatSpec(id: string, updatedAt: string): ChatSpec {
+  return {
+    id,
+    name: "DingTalk chat",
+    session_id: `dingtalk:${id}`,
+    user_id: "u1",
+    channel: "dingtalk",
+    created_at: T0,
+    updated_at: updatedAt,
+    meta: {},
+    status: "idle",
+    pinned: false,
+    archived: false,
+    archived_at: null,
+  } as unknown as ChatSpec;
+}
+
+function makeHistory(
+  turns: Array<{ role: string; text: string }>,
+): ChatHistory {
+  const messages: Message[] = turns.map(
+    ({ role, text }) =>
+      ({
+        role,
+        content: [{ type: "text", text }],
+      }) as unknown as Message,
+  );
+  return { messages, status: "idle" } as unknown as ChatHistory;
+}
+
+afterEach(() => {
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+});
+
+describe("SessionApi converted-cache staleness on updated_at change (#6131)", () => {
+  it("re-fetches messages when the backend updated_at advances", async () => {
+    const id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111";
+    const listSpy = vi
+      .spyOn(api, "listChats")
+      .mockResolvedValue([makeChatSpec(id, T0)]);
+    const getChatSpy = vi
+      .spyOn(api, "getChat")
+      .mockResolvedValue(makeHistory([{ role: "assistant", text: "first" }]));
+
+    // Initial poll + open: fetches history v1 and caches it.
+    await sessionApi.getSessionList();
+    const s1 = await sessionApi.getSession(id);
+    expect(getChatSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    const count1 = (s1.messages || []).length;
+
+    // A new message arrives via DingTalk: backend updated_at advances and the
+    // history now has an extra user turn + reply (distinct cards).
+    listSpy.mockResolvedValue([makeChatSpec(id, T1)]);
+    getChatSpy.mockResolvedValue(
+      makeHistory([
+        { role: "assistant", text: "first" },
+        { role: "user", text: "what time is it" },
+        { role: "assistant", text: "second" },
+      ]),
+    );
+
+    // Poll picks up the newer updated_at, then the user switches back.
+    await sessionApi.getSessionList();
+    const s2 = await sessionApi.getSession(id);
+
+    // Must have re-fetched (cache treated as stale) and show the new message.
+    expect(getChatSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
+    expect((s2.messages || []).length).toBeGreaterThan(count1);
+  });
+
+  it("serves the cache (no re-fetch) when updated_at is unchanged", async () => {
+    const id = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222";
+    vi.spyOn(api, "listChats").mockResolvedValue([makeChatSpec(id, T0)]);
+    const getChatSpy = vi
+      .spyOn(api, "getChat")
+      .mockResolvedValue(makeHistory([{ role: "assistant", text: "only" }]));
+
+    await sessionApi.getSessionList();
+    await sessionApi.getSession(id);
+    expect(getChatSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+
+    // Poll again with the SAME updated_at, then switch back.
+    await sessionApi.getSessionList();
+    await sessionApi.getSession(id);
+
+    // Cache is still valid: no extra network fetch.
+    expect(getChatSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+  });
+});
diff --git a/tests/integration/test_console_chat_updated_at.py b/tests/integration/test_console_chat_updated_at.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..375cb411f2d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/integration/test_console_chat_updated_at.py
@@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+"""Regression test for issue #6131.
+
+After the 2.x migration, sending a message in an existing chat did not
+refresh ``ChatSpec.updated_at``. The console session list sorts by
+``updated_at`` (descending) and polls the backend, so a stale timestamp
+meant the chat never re-surfaced as the most recent conversation.
+
+The fix touches ``updated_at`` inside the console channel's ``stream_one``
+executor (which serves the web-streaming, background-task and terminal
+paths) and inside ``BaseChannel._consume_with_tracker`` (all other
+channels). This test exercises the console web-streaming path end to end
+and asserts that a second message advances ``updated_at`` past the first.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import threading
+import time
+from datetime import datetime
+from http.server import HTTPServer
+
+import httpx
+import pytest
+
+from tests.integration.helpers import (
+    MOCK_LLM_PROVIDER_ID,
+    MockLLMHandler,
+    default_http_timeout,
+    register_mock_provider,
+    unregister_mock_provider,
+)
+
+_HTTP_TIMEOUT = default_http_timeout(15.0)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def mock_llm():
+    """Module-scoped mock OpenAI streaming server."""
+    srv = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), MockLLMHandler)
+    srv.force_error = False
+    srv.force_tool_call = False
+    port = srv.server_address[1]
+    thread = threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True)
+    thread.start()
+    yield srv, f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1"
+    srv.shutdown()
+
+
+def _drain_console_chat(app_server, session_id: str, user_id: str) -> None:
+    """POST /api/console/chat and fully consume the SSE stream.
+
+    Draining to completion guarantees the background producer (which runs
+    ``stream_one``) has finished, so the ``updated_at`` touch is persisted.
+    """
+    body = {
+        "channel": "console",
+        "user_id": user_id,
+        "session_id": session_id,
+        "input": [
+            {
+                "role": "user",
+                "type": "message",
+                "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "hello"}],
+            },
+        ],
+    }
+    url = f"{app_server.base_url}/api/console/chat"
+    with app_server.client.stream(
+        "POST",
+        url,
+        json=body,
+        timeout=httpx.Timeout(20.0, read=20.0),
+    ) as resp:
+        assert resp.status_code == 200, app_server.logs_tail()
+        for _ in resp.iter_lines():
+            pass
+
+
+def _get_chat_updated_at(app_server, session_id: str, user_id: str):
+    """Return (updated_at, created_at) datetimes for the target chat."""
+    resp = app_server.api_request(
+        "GET",
+        "/api/chats",
+        params={"user_id": user_id},
+        timeout=_HTTP_TIMEOUT,
+    )
+    assert resp.status_code == 200, app_server.logs_tail()
+    matches = [c for c in resp.json() if c.get("session_id") == session_id]
+    assert matches, f"chat for session {session_id} not found: {resp.json()}"
+    spec = matches[0]
+    updated = datetime.fromisoformat(spec["updated_at"])
+    created = datetime.fromisoformat(spec["created_at"])
+    return updated, created
+
+
+@pytest.mark.integration
+@pytest.mark.p1
+def test_console_chat_second_message_advances_updated_at(
+    app_server,
+    mock_llm,  # pylint: disable=redefined-outer-name
+) -> None:
+    """A follow-up message must push ``updated_at`` forward (issue #6131).
+
+    API endpoints:
+    - POST /api/console/chat
+    - GET  /api/chats
+    """
+    _srv, mock_url = mock_llm
+    unregister_mock_provider(app_server, MOCK_LLM_PROVIDER_ID)
+    provider_id = register_mock_provider(app_server, mock_url)
+    user_id = "integ-updated-at-6131"
+    session_id = f"console:{user_id}"
+    try:
+        # First message creates the chat and processes a turn.
+        _drain_console_chat(app_server, session_id, user_id)
+        updated_1, created = _get_chat_updated_at(
+            app_server,
+            session_id,
+            user_id,
+        )
+        assert updated_1 >= created
+
+        # Ensure a measurable gap so the comparison is unambiguous.
+        time.sleep(1.2)
+
+        # Second message must refresh updated_at to a later timestamp.
+        _drain_console_chat(app_server, session_id, user_id)
+        updated_2, _ = _get_chat_updated_at(app_server, session_id, user_id)
+
+        assert updated_2 > updated_1, (
+            "updated_at did not advance after the second message: "
+            f"first={updated_1.isoformat()} second={updated_2.isoformat()}"
+        )
+    finally:
+        unregister_mock_provider(app_server, provider_id)

+                next(t for t in tokens if t.is_keyword('dup'))
+                index_token = next(tokens)
+                if not index_token.is_number():
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        "Token following dup in Subrs definition must be a "
+                        f"number, was {index_token}"
+                    )
+                nbytes_token = next(tokens)
+                if not nbytes_token.is_number():
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        "Second token following dup in Subrs definition must "
+                        f"be a number, was {nbytes_token}"
+                    )
+                token = next(tokens)
+                if not token.is_keyword(self._abbr['RD']):
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        f"Token preceding subr must be {self._abbr['RD']}, "
+                        f"was {token}"
+                    )
+                binary_token = tokens.send(1+nbytes_token.value())
+                entries[index_token.value()] = binary_token.value()
+        except StopIteration:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "Malformed Type1 font file: Incomplete /Subrs"
+            ) from None
+
+        # The indices must cover 0 to count-1 exactly.
+        if (len(entries) != count
+                or (count and (min(entries), max(entries)) != (0, count - 1))):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "Malformed Type1 font file: /Subrs indices do not cover "
+                f"0 to {count - 1}"
+            )
+        array = [entries[index] for index in range(count)]
 
         return array, next(tokens).endpos()

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: Type1Font allocates /Subrs array from declared count before validating the body
problem_statement.body:
### Bug summary

The Type1 font parser trusts the declared `/Subrs` count and allocates a Python list of that size before validating that the following body actually contains that many subroutine definitions. A compact malformed Type1 font can therefore cause avoidable large allocation before parsing fails.


### Code for reproduction

```Python
import pathlib
import resource
import tempfile
import time

from matplotlib._type1font import Type1Font


def main():
    subrs_count = 5_000_000

    plaintext = (
        b"/FontName /LargeSubrsCount def\n"
        b"/FontBBox [0 0 1 1] def\n"
        + f"/Subrs {subrs_count} array\n".encode("ascii")
    )

    encrypted_hex = Type1Font._encrypt(plaintext, "eexec").hex().encode("ascii")
    pfa = (
        b"%!PS-AdobeFont-1.0: LargeSubrsCount 001.000\n"
        b"eexec\n"
        + encrypted_hex
        + b"\n"
        + (b"0" * 512)
        + b"\ncleartomark\n"
    )

    font_path = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "large-subrs-count.pfa"
    font_path.write_bytes(pfa)

    rss_before = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
    start = time.time()
    try:
        Type1Font(str(font_path))
    except StopIteration:
        parse_result = "body_rejected_after_allocation"
    except MemoryError:
        parse_result = "memory_error"
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("malformed font unexpectedly parsed")

    elapsed = time.time() - start
    rss_after = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss

    print(f"subrs_count={subrs_count}")
    print(f"parse_result={parse_result}")
    print(f"elapsed_seconds={elapsed:.3f}")
    print(f"rss_before_kb={rss_before}")
    print(f"rss_after_kb={rss_after}")
    print(f"rss_delta_kb={rss_after - rss_before}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Actual outcome

In a source-checkout verification run, a compact generated PFA declaring `/Subrs 5000000 array` caused the parser to allocate based on the declared count before the malformed body was rejected:

```text
subrs_count=5000000
parse_result=body_rejected_after_allocation
elapsed_seconds=0.009
rss_before_kb=45168
rss_after_kb=84208
rss_delta_kb=39040
```


### Expected outcome

Matplotlib should validate the `/Subrs` body structure before allocating a count-sized list, or enforce a reasonable maximum `/Subrs` count before allocation.

### Additional information


The relevant parser path is `lib/matplotlib/_type1font.py`:

```python
def _parse_subrs(self, tokens, _data):
    count_token = next(tokens)
    ...
    count = count_token.value()
    array = [None] * count
    next(t for t in tokens if t.is_keyword('array'))
```

The allocation happens immediately after reading the count token. The parser only confirms the `array` keyword and the following `dup` entries after the list has already been allocated.

This report is intended as a robustness bug, not as a security vulnerability report. It requires processing an untrusted Type1 PFA/PFB font.


### Operating system

Linux

### Matplotlib Version

main branch source checkout; reproduced on commit `5a33910eb7827d8a6188ff42bc788951c015ff48`; same parser shape was still present on current `main` commit `996f4e877f6a7a50a68e00879183b8db8761461d`.

### Matplotlib Backend

Not backend-specific

### Python version

Python 3.12

### Jupyter version

Not applicable

### Installation

git checkout

problem_statement.title: perf: vectorize a loop-based matrix constructor
problem_statement.body:
A few small matrix constructors build their result with a Python `for` loop over a preallocated `np.zeros`/`np.empty`, where numpy vectorization would be faster and clearer.

### What to do
Pick ONE of the following and replace its loop with a vectorized construction:
- `toqito/matrices/standard_basis.py`
- `toqito/matrices/gen_pauli_z.py`
- `toqito/matrices/entangled_subspace.py`
- `toqito/perms/perfect_matchings.py`

### Requirements
- The output must be bit-for-bit identical to the current implementation. Keep the existing test, and add a case comparing the new output to the previous one if helpful.
- Include a measured speedup on a representative size (a short `timeit` snippet in the PR description is enough).
- Do not change the function's signature or behavior.

This one needs some numpy comfort, so it is a good pick if you want a slightly meatier first PR.

### Verifying
```
uv run pytest toqito/matrices/tests toqito/perms/tests
```
